title: Savings Percentage
summary: Validated savings divided by addressable spend or baseline spend.
formula: Validated savings divided by addressable spend or baseline spend.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.

Tie movement to an operating playbook and weekly cadence.

articleSections.title: Strategic Context & Value Driver
body: In the realm of private equity procurement, Savings Percentage is the primary barometer for the efficiency of the strategic sourcing function. It measures the delta between the 'baseline' spend and the newly negotiated 'contracted' spend, serving as a critical indicator of the 'Procurement Alpha' being generated during the hold period. For an Operating Partner, achieving a high savings percentage is not just about cost-cutting; it is about validating the investment thesis's margin expansion assumptions and demonstrating the GP's ability to drive operational excellence.

We view savings percentage as a leading indicator of EBITDA growth. In the first 12-18 months of an LBO, the procurement workstream is often the fastest engine for value creation, as it requires less capital investment than revenue-side initiatives. By tracking savings across every category, we create a 'Value Bridge' that connects the initial acquisition price to the terminal value, providing the board with a clear view of how much 'multiple arbitrage' is being created through internal cost optimization versus external market multiple expansion.

The strategic importance of this metric is amplified in inflationary environments. A business that can consistently deliver a positive savings percentage even as input costs rise is a business that possesses a superior 'Procurement Moat.' By institutionalizing a rigorous sourcing process, we ensure that the portfolio company is always capturing the best possible market terms, protecting its gross margins and ensuring that its pricing power is used to expand profits rather than just to keep pace with inflation.
articleSections.callout: Savings percentage is the 'Yield' of your procurement engine—high performance here is the fastest route to EBITDA expansion.

articleSections.title: Operational Levers & Benchmarking
body: The primary operational levers for maximizing savings percentage include 'Competitive Bidding' (RFPs), 'Vendor Consolidation,' and 'Demand Management.' We benchmark savings percentages against industry norms, typically targeting 8-12% for direct materials and 15-25% for fragmented indirect categories like facilities, shipping, and marketing. Any significant underperformance against these benchmarks suggests a 'Soft' sourcing process that is failing to market-test the vendor base effectively or is leaving money on the table through poor negotiation tactics.

A critical lever is the 'Total Cost of Ownership' (TCO) lens. We move the organization beyond 'Unit Price' and toward a holistic view that includes logistics, inventory carrying costs, and quality-related scrap. By benchmarking the TCO rather than just the invoice price, we identify 'Hidden Savings' that are often overlooked by traditional procurement teams. This sophisticated approach allows the Operating Partner to drive deeper structural savings that are more resilient to market fluctuations and provide a true long-term competitive advantage for the portfolio company.

Benchmarking also extends to the 'Sourcing Cycle Time.' We track how long it takes to go from 'Opportunity Identification' to 'Contract Signing,' with a goal of running high-impact RFPs in 60-90 days. Slow cycle times erode the 'Run-Rate' savings in a given fiscal year, reducing the immediate impact on EBITDA. By professionalizing the sourcing workflow and utilizing specialized RFP tools, we accelerate the realization of savings and ensure that the 'Value Creation Momentum' is maintained throughout the hold period. Benchmarking is the 'Pace-Setter' for the procurement function.

articleSections.title: Math & Unit Economics (Example Injection)
body: Consider a $500M revenue consumer goods business with $200M in annual direct and indirect spend. The Operating Partner initiates a 'Procurement Wave' targeting 75% of that spend—$150M—across 12 core categories. Initial benchmarking suggests a potential 10% average savings percentage across the wave. If successfully executed, this workstream will add $15M to the company's EBITDA on an annualized basis, which flows directly to the bottom line with 100% margin efficiency.

The unit economics of this effort are highly attractive. Engaging a specialized procurement consultancy to run the wave might cost $750k in fees plus a 10% 'success fee' on first-year savings ($1.5M). The total investment of $2.25M yields a $15M return in the first year alone—a nearly 7x 'Cash-on-Cash' return. More importantly, this $15M of EBITDA becomes 'Permament' profit that is capitalized at the exit, creating massive enterprise value that far outweighs the one-time implementation costs.

At a 12x exit multiple, that 10% savings percentage ($15M EBITDA) is worth $180M in enterprise value. If the GP had failed to execute this workstream and only achieved a 3% savings rate ($4.5M), they would have 'lost' $126M of potential EV. This math highlights why the savings percentage is a 'High-Leverage' metric; even small basis-point improvements in the savings rate translate into tens of millions of dollars in final transaction value, making it a central pillar of the 'Operational Alpha' narrative.

articleSections.title: Technology & Tooling Stack
body: To manage and track savings with professional rigor, we deploy a 'Savings Tracking' platform like SpendHQ's Performance Management or GEP Smart's Savings Tracker. These tools provide a 'Centralized Dashboard' where every sourcing project is logged, from the 'Pipeline' stage to 'Realized' savings in the P&L. By moving away from decentralized spreadsheets, we create a 'Single Source of Truth' that allows the Operating Partner and the CFO to monitor the impact of procurement initiatives in real-time and verify that the savings are actually hitting the financial statements.

We also utilize 'e-Sourcing' and 'e-Auction' platforms like Scout RFP (Workday) or Keelvar to run the competitive bidding process. These tools allow us to conduct high-velocity RFPs and 'Reverse Auctions' where vendors compete in real-time on price and terms. This 'Digital Auction' environment often drives an incremental 3-5% in savings over traditional negotiation methods by creating a transparent and highly competitive market for the company's business. Digitizing the sourcing process is essential for achieving 'Best-in-Market' pricing at scale.

Finally, we integrate these tools with 'Spend Analytics' software like SpendHQ to perform 'Baseline Audits.' This ensures that the 'before' and 'after' data are comparable and that the reported savings percentage is not inflated by volume shifts or category re-classifications. This level of data integrity is critical for maintaining credibility with the board and the future buyer's due diligence team. By institutionalizing a data-driven savings tracking process, we create a 'Value Trail' that is easily auditable and highly defensible during the exit process.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness & Multiple Expansion
body: During the exit, a documented track record of high savings percentages is a powerful indicator of a 'Sophisticated' and 'Professionally Managed' procurement function. Prospective buyers will scrutinize the 'Savings Bridge' to ensure that the EBITDA expansion is the result of structural cost improvements rather than one-time 'windfalls' or temporary price concessions. By presenting a multi-year history of consistent savings capture, we prove that the business has a 'Repeatable Process' for driving margin expansion that can be maintained by the next owner.

We often include a 'Procurement Maturity Assessment' in the VDR, highlighting how the savings percentage has evolved as the company's sourcing capabilities have professionalized. This level of transparency reduces the 'Operational Risk' for the buyer, potentially accelerating the transaction timeline and supporting a premium multiple. It demonstrates that the business has a 'Self-Optimizing' cost structure that is not dependent on GP-led intervention, making it a highly attractive 'Platform' for further growth or buy-and-build strategies.

Ultimately, the savings percentage contributes to multiple expansion by de-risking the 'Cost-Side' of the P&L and proving 'Operating Leverage.' A business that consistently achieves >10% savings on its addressable spend is seen as having more 'Predictable Earnings' and better 'Margin Protection' than one where costs are unmanaged. By elevating savings percentage from a tactical metric to a core strategic pillar, we maximize the 'Terminal Value' of the asset and deliver superior returns to our LPs, cementing the Operating Partner's reputation as a world-class value creator.
